ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory vetting of all directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canada’s autonomous sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and, as a bank-acceptance condition, the United States OFAC SDN List; PEP identification is mandatory under FINTRAC reporting rules for politically exposed persons, both domestic and foreign, with ongoing monitoring and enhanced due diligence for higher-risk jurisdictions connected to cross-border procurements

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, the corporate name must be prepared in French, and a foreign-language name must be accompanied by a French version in the company’s constitutional documents; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into roman characters for registry searchability; approved corporate designations include 'Société par actions' and English equivalents such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' provided the French version is displayed
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term implying royal, governmental, or official sponsorship
Any term contrary to public order or indicating an illicit activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name refusal by the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant, through counsel, may file a written application for administrative review within 30 days of the refusal decision; if the Registraire maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Québec within 30 days of the review decision; interim name reservations may be renewed procedurally before expiry by filing a new reservation request containing the same name, but the same prohibitions continue to apply

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a wholesale matcha distribution company provided the virtual office provides a physical address in Quebec, a named person for service of process, and access to corporate records at that address; pure postal-box addresses are not compliant. As the business model is non-retail and low-risk, a virtual office is generally accepted for due diligence, but if Canadian Food Inspection Agency registration becomes necessary for importing food products, a physical warehouse or filing address must be added.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 2–5% annual probability). Registered office location is a public registry entry, and unannounced inspections are usually triggered by consumer complaints, customs alerts, or tax discrepancies; for a low-risk category without a statutory operating licence, routine physical inspection is unlikely but not impossible.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-48, 97-123; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 9-143
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar); Corporations Canada for federal charter
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation / Déclaration immatriculation (Articles de constitution)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required for a Business Corporation in Canada or Quebec; share consideration may be money, property, or past services, and must be fully accounted for in the corporate share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the corporation hereby adopts its Articles of Incorporation as filed with the competent registry and approves the initial share subscription reflected in the share certificate register. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office be established at [registered address], Quebec, and the designated legal controller be mandated. FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Name A] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name B] be appointed Treasurer, and [Name C] be appointed Corporate Secretary, each authorized to execute banking agreements, trade contracts, and regulatory filings. All officers are hereby delegated authority to complete any ancillary documents necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name approval and corporate name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal; NUANS name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS/REQ name search to confirm the proposed corporate name is available in Quebec. Submit a name reservation request through the REQ online service or deliver a paper declaration to a REQ service point. Ensure any approved name is reserved for the statutory period prior to articles filing.
required_dossiers: Statutory declaration of name use if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or challenged, file a revised name request with supporting trademark coexistence evidence or a consent letter from the similarly named entity, or select a distinctive alternative name within the reservation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel and the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation, by-laws, initial director consent, and registered office designation. Have all incorporators execute the articles and initial by-laws. Ensure the corporate share structure and authorized share classes comply with the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Canada Business Corporations Act if federal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal deficiency in the draft documents and re-execute; if a directorial consent is missing, obtain fresh signatures and file a corrected consent with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) or Corporations Canada (if federal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Articles of Incorporation and supporting documents online via REQ's 'Immatriculation d'une personne morale' service, or via Corporations Canada's online filing center for a federal corporation. Pay the statutory filing fee using a government-approved payment method. Retain the electronic acknowledgement and the assigned incorporation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of deficiency, respond within 30 days by amending the articles or supplying supplementary declarations; void the initial filing and resubmit a complete package if the deficiency is fundamental.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the initial organizational meeting of directors. Adopt by-laws, appoint officers, fix the capital subscription, approve the corporate seal, and adopt the registered office. Document all decisions in written minutes. Issue share certificates in accordance with the authorized share structure and record consideration received.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a vacancy in director or officer positions occurs at formation, call a special board meeting, obtain a written waiver of notice, and appoint replacement individuals by ordinary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office, records, and statutory registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), provincial tax authorizes, and local municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office address and update the REQ declarative register. Obtain a Quebec establishment number (NEQ), register for GST/QST with Revenu Québec, obtain a federal business number from the CRA, and register with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for payroll/occupational safety where applicable. Open the corporate bank account and maintain statutory corporate records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or payroll registration is delayed or rejected, contact Revenu Québec or CRA to request accelerated processing; provide a letter of explanation and any missing supporting documentation within 15 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation operational registrations and licensing verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ), Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), and local industrial safety boards
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify whether any sector-specific licenses are required for wholesaling organic matcha powder. If the activity includes import or interprovincial trade of food, apply for a Basic Food Import License under the Safe Food for Canadians Act. If the activity includes storing, handling, or repackaging food in Quebec, obtain MAPAQ food establishment authorization. Maintain documentary proof of organic certification and ensure any warehouse or distribution facility complies with municipal zoning and fire safety regulations.
required_dossiers: Proof of organic certification (e.g. GOTS, USDA Organic, Canada Organic Regime conformity)
Municipal zoning and fire safety certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a license application is refused or queried, submit a corrected food safety plan or organic certification evidence, request an informal hearing with MAPAQ/CFIA, and if necessary obtain a court order or compliance agreement to resume lawful operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ) and Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Authorization / Certificat d'établissement alimentaire (when storing, handling, or repackaging food); Basic Import License under the Safe Food for Canadians Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt — minimal wholesale storage and repackaging activities are typically exempt from a full environmental impact assessment, but may require an attestation or registration under municipal effluent and waste bylaws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet municipal sewer bylaw limits for BOD, TSS, pH, and grease; any VOC emissions from cleaning or packaging processes must be within local state-of-the-art air pollution limits; integral waste handling must meet provincial residual materials management regulations (REIMR).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local municipal fire prevention service, structural load inspection certificate for any warehousing racks, and CNESST workplace clearance confirming worker safety and occupational health compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Québec – https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entities carrying on business in Canada must apply for a CRA Business Number (BN) via the Business Registration Online (BRO) platform or by completing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number). For GST/HST registration, a non-resident may register voluntarily under Division V of the Excise Tax Act. For QST, a non-resident must also register with Revenu Québec (Form LM-1 or online via Revenu Québec’s Business Registration Service), typically requiring a Quebec establishment or an agent, and must obtain a QST registration number. Prior to registration, the entity must have a Canadian-representative appointment for service of process if no place of business in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian Business Corporation is a resident taxpayer if incorporated in Canada or managed/controlled in Canada; subject to Part I federal income tax and Quebec corporate tax under the Taxation Act (Quebec)).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists for Canadian federal tax purposes. A corporation may elect under subsection 216(1) of the Income Tax Act to be taxed on net Canadian-source employment income, but this is irrelevant for a trading corporation. Hybrid mismatch elections under OECD BEPS Action 2 are not applicable as domestic law follows the nexus approach. For GST/HST, a non-resident may elect to use the simplified 'quick method' for small suppliers; for QST, an election for the 'general rate' may apply to certain taxable benefits, but no deemed classification election analogous to the U.S. check-the-box is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal) and QST (Quebec) – value-added tax regimes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST and QST small-supplier thresholds); once exceeded, registration is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate currently applies federally or in Quebec. However, GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 10 million must file GST/HST returns electronically; Quebec imposes mandatory electronic filing for QST returns for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1,500,000. Standard electronic data interchange (EDI) or XML-based invoicing is accepted, but no authorized clearance portal, API submission, or Hash-based stamping regime exists for the ordinary sale of goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible personal property (including organic matcha powder) are zero-rated under section 39 of the Excise Tax Act (GST/HST) and equivalent provisions of Quebec’s QST legislation, provided the goods are exported within a reasonable time, usually within 60 days of sale, by the supplier or the purchaser, and the supplier retains documentary proof of export. Services are zero-rated if performed for a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST/QST and the service is not rendered to a recipient physically present in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13A / Goods to Follow list)
Bill of Lading (or air waybill) showing Canadian origin and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating and reassess GST/HST and QST along with penalties and interest. The Excise Tax Act imposes a penalty of 10% of the net tax owing on failure to remit, plus interest; false statements or omissions may trigger a $8,000 or 50% of the tax sought to be evaded penalty under subsection 285.1(1) ETA. Quebec’s Tax Administration Act similarly authorizes penalties of 10%–25% of the amount evaded and retroactive assessments up to four years (seven years in cases of negligence, wilful default, or fraud). Evidence of fraudulent export documentation or sham repatriation also leads to criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act and Criminal Code, and clawback of refunds received under section 296 ETA.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator of federally chartered deposit-taking institutions; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the financial intelligence unit and AML authority. Canada does not operate a dedicated foreign exchange control bureau; the Canadian dollar trades on a free float and there is no central exchange-control approval regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange-control licences, no prior approvals for capital injections, no restrictions on dividend or profit remittance to non-resident shareholders, and no requirement to justify foreign-currency inflows to the central bank. Legal obligations on remittance are limited to tax at source under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (generally 25% on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to treaty reduction), Quebec-specific corporate formalities, and FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction or Suspicious Transaction Reporting above prescribed thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender of export receipts. A Quebec matcha distribution corporation may retain foreign currency in a permissible foreign-currency operating account, convert it at negotiated bank rates, or net positions subject to general tax accounting. Export proceeds remain taxable in Canada and foreign exchange gains or losses must be recorded according to IFRS or ASPE in Canadian-dollar functional statements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. A Quebec corporation may use fintech electronic money institution (EMI) interfaces, but in Canada such providers must operate either as a FINTRAC-registered money services business (MSB), a payment service provider under an regulated Canadian bank partnership, or a non-bank financial institution appropriately authorized by provincial law. Unregulated offshore EMIs are not viable as a primary treasury host for SWIFT and trade settlements because Canadian banks will still require a direct relationship for clearing, trade documentation, and FX risk management. The optimal strategy is to use a Schedule I bank as the settlement spine and optionally connect a FINTRAC-compliant fintech to initiate payment requests or operational dashboards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no federal statutory rule requiring directors to appear physically at a Canadian bank branch. FINTRAC permits remote identification through verified digital identity mechanisms, and most Schedule I banks support video KYC and electronic document execution for private corporations. In practice, for a newly incorporated Quebec distribution entity, the bank may require one specific due-diligence intake meeting by video or in person, especially where non-resident ownership is present. The Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), notice of legal publicity, certificate of incorporation, and evidence of registered office will be required. Remote account opening is achievable but should assume a documented beneficial-ownership interview and bank-specific enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated wholesale activity of organic matcha distribution and a sudden large-volume, multi-jurisdiction wire pattern without underlying trade documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction ladder comprising purchase orders, supplier invoices and licences, organic certification, bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs entry documents, bank wire confirmations, and a treasury narrative reconciling each Canadian-dollar and foreign-currency movement to an open purchase order or contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a non-resident related party or offshore holding company into a newly opened Quebec account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company certificate, register of directors and beneficial owners, intercompany loan agreement or board resolution for share capital, source-of-wealth statement, audited financial statements of the contributor, tax form NR301 or NR302 where applicable, notarized passport and address verification for each beneficial owner, and no prior regulatory sanctions record for the remitting entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade payments routed to jurisdictions flagged by FINTRAC or global sanctions lists as high-risk or with limited information exchange
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier export and phytosanitary licences, Japan Organic Matcha certificate or regional JAS equivalent, OECD-Halal/cGMP line of certification where relevant, proof of sanctions and PEP screening for all counterparties, bank-confirmed negative media search, vessel or courier tracking evidence, and a supply-chain affidavit identifying the physical origin and logistics chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of multiple foreign-currency accounts or frequent FX forward transactions without a clear corporate treasury mandate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes or treasury policy explicitly authorizing FX hedging, appointment of the signatory treasury officer, bank ISDA and credit support documentation, a monthly derivatives exposure report, profit and loss analysis showing hedge accounting connected to commercial maturities, and bank counterparty suitability confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque layered ownership through Quebec holding companies, trusts, or non-Canadian parent structures, making beneficial ownership unclear
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified CBCA or Quebec company act birth certificate; attestation from the enterprise registrar showing current directors; ultimate beneficial owner declaration with percentage ownership; formal corporate chart; tax returns or financial statements; notarized identity documents; and an explanation of the commercial rationale for the exact entity structure selected.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound shareholder capital or related-party loans via SWIFT MT103 to the Quebec corporation's operating or capital account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The wire should state the beneficiary account number and SWIFT BIC, and Field 70 or the payment narrative must include the reference 'Capital injection – ISIC 4631 organic matcha distribution' or similar clear purpose, because Canada does not require a government-issued exchange-control code but banks and FINTRAC rely on the narrative to assess legitimacy. If the inbound remittance exceeds CAD 10,000 in cash equivalents or triggers suspicion, the bank is obliged to file a Large Cash Transaction Report or Suspicious Transaction Report. No prior central-bank approval is required. All contributions should be recorded in corporate accounts and reflected in the Quebec enterprise register as either paid-in share capital or an intercompany liability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for matcha procurement should be settled through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for standard commercial invoices and open-account terms, or through a commercial documentary Letter of Credit (LC) under UCP 600 and ISBP 745 for larger, recurring purchase programs. A Canadian bank will issue or confirm the LC after reviewing the trade contract, LC mandate, and credit limit. For domestic or North American settlements, Payments Canada provides clearing in Canadian dollars; for USD, the Canadian bank uses its U.S. correspondent through Fedwire or CHIPS. Each disbursement must be matched to the commercial invoice, the supplier's banking details, the organic matcha certificate, and the bill of lading; these documents are retained in the compliance file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank, with tenors aligned to predicted A/R and A/P cycles in USD, JPY, EUR, or CAD; the corporation must execute an ISDA or bank FX master agreement and provide board authorization and evidence of underlying trade exposure.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for currencies without fully functional onshore deliverability, where the supplier invoice is denominated in such a currency; the hedging rationale and bank counterparty suitability must be documented, and any NDF rollover must be approved by the treasury committee.

Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD or CAD/JPY) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement to convert a foreign-currency trade liability or capital borrowing into Canadian dollar obligations; because swaps extend beyond simple spot or forward contracts, the Quebec corporation must have adequate capital, board authorization, and bank credit approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or continuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No annual late fee imposed; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution after written notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 per 30-day period, up to CAD 1,000; registration may be struck off after three consecutive years of default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the taxation year-end; for a calendar year-end, due June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months); repeat failures may attract an additional 10% penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the taxation year-end; for a calendar year-end, due June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest on any balance due; continued failure may lead to assessment and collection actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based mandatory audit threshold for a private business corporation; an independent licensed auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders entitled to vote consent to waive the appointment. Public corporations and securities-law-regulated entities are subject to mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook; Quebec does not prescribe a separate local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's Registraire des entreprises requires beneficial-owner information to be verified and updated in the annual declaration. Under the Canada Business Corporations Act, an internal register of individuals with significant control must be maintained at the registered office and updated within 15 days of any change; the federal annual return confirms whether such a register is in place.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150-400 USD (including registered office address and annual agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-8,000 USD for a small private corporation if audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate: 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec provincial 11.5%); non-resident corporations taxed only on Canadian-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; preferential small business deduction available to an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) reducing the federal rate to 9% and Quebec rate to 3.2% on the first C$500,000 of active business income; SR&ED refundable investment tax credits; accelerated capital cost allowance on qualified property; Quebec tax credits for innovation and manufacturing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; CRA Corporations Tax Online / EFILE through certified tax preparation software or Represent a Client.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal period normally cannot exceed 12 months without CRA authorization.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File no later than six months after fiscal year-end. Tax balance due by the balance-due day: two months after year-end for a non-CCPC; three months after year-end for an eligible CCPC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA business number (BN) issued at incorporation; all corporate accounts (payroll, GST/HST, corporate tax) are rolled under this unique identifier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must obtain a CRA BN through the Non-Resident Corporation number application before filing; do not enter a foreign tax ID in the BN field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The actual last day of the corporation's fiscal period in YYYY-MM-DD format; determines all deadlines and loss apportionment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian fiscal period end exactly as reflected in the books; a non-resident that changes its foreign year-end must seek CRA approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after Part I adjustments, loss carryovers and any applicable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income taxable in Canada under Part I (business income earned through a Canadian permanent establishment and certain Canadian-source property income). Attach the required non-resident schedules and allocation computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculates gross Part I federal tax, the 10% provincial abatement, the 13% general rate reduction, small business deduction and federal tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents use Schedule 1 to compute tax on Canadian-source active business income; do not claim the provincial abatement for income not allocated to a Canadian province unless a permanent establishment exists in a province.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records non-capital loss carryback/carryforward balances, expiry years and inter-jurisdictional tax carryover computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Schedule 4 for a non-resident should include only Canadian-source loss balances and must be consistent with the Part I taxable income return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Income Tax Act s.162(2): 5% of the assessed unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month of delay up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty doubles the rates to 10% plus 2% per month up to 24 months. Daily compounding interest is also charged at prescribed quarterly rates on unpaid corporate tax balances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed with Revenu Québec via the Clic Revenu secure electronic portal or Revenu Québec-certified EDI software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal period must correspond to the fiscal period used on the federal T2 return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File no later than six months after fiscal year-end. The balance of Quebec income tax is due two months after year-end, extended to three months for a qualifying SME under Revenu Québec administrative practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenu Québec file number and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) issued by the Registraire des entreprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required only if the corporation has a permanent establishment in Quebec or earns income from Quebec property; all other non-residents must file the CO-17 in limited Quebec-source income situations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income computed from federal taxable income, adjusted for Quebec-specific deductions and provincial allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate taxable income to Quebec using the Quebec permanent establishment attribution rules where the non-resident corporation has establishments in more than one province.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Quebec corporate income tax applying the 11.5% general rate before credits and reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident, line 9 reflects tax on Quebec-source income attributable to the permanent establishment; claim federal/provincial treaty-based allocations only if substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule of Tax Credits / Loss Carryovers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records Quebec loss carryover usage, foreign tax credits and refundable or utilisable Quebec tax credits (e.g., innovation, production).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim only Quebec-recognized tax credits connected to Quebec income and cannot offset foreign-source losses against Quebec taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under the Tax Administration Act: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month, up to 12%; repeated failure triggers a 10% base penalty plus 2% per month up to 24 months. Revenu Québec also applies prescribed interest and can issue reminder and demand letters with additional recovery costs.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident dividend recipients must submit a valid certificate of residency (tax residence certificate) to the Canadian payer and/or CRA and file CRA Form NR301 (Non-Resident Claim for Treaty Reduced Rate of Withholding) before the payment is made. The payer then withholds at the treaty rate. If the NR301 is filed late, the non-resident may apply for a refund/reassessment on the Canadian T2 or NR4 process within the statutory limitation periods. Treaty benefits are subject to beneficial ownership and the limitation-on-benefits/principal-purpose test found in Canada's tax conventions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for both interest and royalties paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident. Treaties commonly reduce royalties to 10%–15% and interest to 0%–15% (e.g., Article X and XI of the Canada–China DTA: interest 10%, royalties 10%); Quebec does not impose a separate provincial withholding tax on cross-border interest or royalty payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents) is mandatory if the aggregate value of reportable non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with each non-resident is greater than C$1,000,000 per fiscal year. Contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (Local File/Master File, OECD-aligned under CRA administrative practice) must be prepared and retained by taxpayers with total group revenue above C$50,000,000 and should be updated before the T2 filing deadline.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute of the type used in offshore financial centres; however, substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), the concept of central management and control for corporate residence, and treaty anti-abuse clauses. A Quebec corporation importing and distributing matcha powder must maintain real decision-making, staff, premises and risk functions in Canada; a passive shell with management and books outside Canada may be deemed to be a non-resident or a sham and denied treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to report Canadian matcha powder sales, suppressing revenue, creating backdated supplier invoices from offshore related parties, or operating an undisclosed parallel book for wire-transfer payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross-negligence penalty under Income Tax Act s.163(2): 50% of the federal tax understated; criminal tax evasion under s.239(1) carries a fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years. Quebec administrative penalties mirror federal treatment and add provincial interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly direct or assist the misstatement are parties to the offence under s.242 of the Income Tax Act; they face personal criminal liability, fines, restitution orders, and imprisonment without corporate-veil protection. Travel bans can be imposed as bail/court conditions during prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Quebec-registered corporation with no local office, no resident director control, no accounting records in Canada, and booking the matcha distribution profit through a paper subsidiary to obtain low-tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may re-determine corporate residence under the central-management-and-control test and GAAR, deny treaty/Limited Liability benefits, reassess income in the hands of the true beneficial owner, and levy Part XIII withholding on deemed dividends. Persistent non-compliance leads to administrative dissolution under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and loss of registration with the Registraire des entreprises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false statutory declarations or permit unlawful dissolution are jointly liable for unpaid corporate income tax, GST/QST and source deductions; courts may impose asset-freezing orders, travel bans and orders requiring personal restitution before the corporate veil can be lifted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling ceremonial matcha powder to a related Hong Kong or Singapore distributor below arm's-length prices, paying excessive management fees to an offshore affiliate, or failing to keep contemporaneous comparability and method documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjusts the transaction to arm's-length under Income Tax Act s.247(2) and imposes a transfer-pricing penalty under s.247(3) equal to 10% of the gross adjustment. The taxpayer also faces T106 late/incomplete information-return penalties up to C$2,500 per year plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed personally for tax liabilities arising from deliberate transfer-pricing misrepresentation when they signed the T2/CO-17 or directed the pricing; criminal culpability is possible if the understatement is intentional, with fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring large Swift TT and wire transfers to suppliers in amounts below thresholds, mixing trade payments with personal accounts, or moving matcha proceeds through the corporation without a traceable audit trail and suspicious transaction review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, FINTRAC may impose administrative monetary penalties up to C$1,000,000 per noncompliance for a corporation; criminal money-laundering under Criminal Code s.462.31 carries imprisonment up to ten years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director designated as a compliance officer can be personally fined for failure to implement an adequate anti-money-laundering program; courts may order travel bans and passport surrender where there is a flight risk, plus confiscation of illicit assets under the Criminal Code.
